rule.description: Packet-layer code maintains the shared wire-activity accounting record directly instead of delegating the update to the module which owns the record. The rule identifies the record structurally (externally-linked file-scope state maintained by a function in a module which does not define it, in write position: assignment left-hand side, increment or decrement, or address-of handoff), so renaming neither hides a violation nor falsifies a conforming repair.

checks.description: Detect functions outside the owning module that directly maintain the wire-activity accounting record: each detection is one affected function, reported at its first direct maintenance statement.
checks.detected_relation: packet-layer function -> direct maintenance (write, step, or handoff) of externally-owned shared accounting state
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The accounting policy for the record belongs to the module which defines it; when update code is scattered across packet functions, one conceptual change to the accounting must be inspected and edited at every such function, which is the given smell type for this case.

matches.evidence: clears the session-scoped record fields in a local loop, then counts a session start and tallies the sent CONNECT packet and its wire bytes inline at the end of connect serialization
increments the received CONNACK counter and accumulates the inbound wire byte total directly after reading the session flags
steps the sent counter for the zero-length packet type and adds the wire length inline in the shared keep-alive and disconnect serializer
server-side connect decoding counts the received CONNECT packet and its inbound wire bytes directly inside the version-valid branch
publish serialization steps the sent PUBLISH counter, adds the wire length and payload bytes, and refreshes the payload high-water mark inline
publish delivery counts the received PUBLISH packet and inbound wire bytes, accumulates payload bytes, and updates the payload high-water mark inline
ack decoding tallies the received packet type and wire bytes inline on the success path, and steps the reject total directly when a truncated body is turned away
subscribe serialization steps the sent SUBSCRIBE counter and accumulates the wire byte total inline
suback decoding counts the received SUBACK packet, its wire bytes, and the number of granted-QoS entries decoded directly
server-side subscribe decoding counts the received SUBSCRIBE packet, its wire bytes, and how many topic filters were decoded, inline
suback serialization steps the sent SUBACK counter and adds its wire length directly
unsubscribe serialization steps the sent UNSUBSCRIBE counter and accumulates the wire bytes inline
unsubscribe decoding steps the reject total directly on a truncated filter list, and on success counts the received packet, its wire bytes, and decoded filter multiplicity inline
unsuback serialization steps the sent UNSUBACK counter and adds its wire length directly
the blocking read path steps the accepted-frame counter directly once a complete frame has been assembled from the transport
the non-blocking state machine steps the accepted-frame counter directly in the case which completes a frame
before dispatching on packet type, the client-view formatter writes the inspected packet type into the record's viewport field inline
before dispatching on packet type, the server-view formatter writes the inspected packet type into the record's viewport field inline

excluded.reason: conforming contrast: delegates its accounting through the owning module's public entry point rather than maintaining the record inline; references to the module's API are not the violation and must not be detected.

the record's defining translation unit is its owner; housekeeping inside the owning module is the intended design and is excluded wherever the module ends up (the exclusion is by definition-site ownership, not by the file name alone).
read-only references to shared state (examining a count or setting without writing it) are not maintenance and are not part of this relation.
function-local statics and state defined by the same translation unit are maintained by their own module and fall outside this cross-module relation.
